name: The Rienzi Yaupon
verified_sources: Texas Big Tree Registry, Texas A&M Forest Service, TreeID 1128 (state champion class, circumference 36 in / 91 cm, spread 28.5 ft, height 31 ft, condition code 3, owner of record Rienzi/Museum of Fine Arts Houston, PublicOrPrivate=1, Display=1, MEASURED AUGUST 2024, one of the most recently re-measured trees in this batch)

Houston Chronicle's Azalea Trail coverage of Rienzi's gardens, independently describing yaupons as part of the garden's evergreen structure at this site; mfah.org's own Rienzi visiting-hours page confirms the four-acre garden is free and open for self-guided visits daily except Sundays before 1pm and the whole month of August
access: Free. Rienzi's gardens are open for self-guided walking every day, Mon-Sat 10am-4:30pm and Sun 1-4:30pm, no ticket or reservation needed for the garden itself (only the house tour is reservation-based). Closed the entire month of August.
transport: In central Houston (River Oaks), roughly 5 km from downtown; walkable from nearby Kirby Dr bus stops.
verify_notes: Only ONE source names this exact specimen (the state registry), which does however carry a very recent measurement (August 2024), the best 'alive now' evidence in this whole batch. A second search found the Houston Chronicle independently confirming yaupons are part of Rienzi's planted garden structure at this address, and MFAH's own site confirms free self-guided garden access, but neither names this individual champion-class plant, so per the two-attempts rule this ships flagged rather than chased further (a third search of TCLF's Rienzi landscape page found beech, magnolia, oak and loblolly pine named but not yaupon specifically). No age documented and none derived: yaupon holly is usually a large shrub rather than a timber tree, and no published growth-rate figure for it was found this pass. The four-acre garden means the registry point is treated as approximate pending an on-site pin.

name: The Russ Pitman Mexican White Oak
species: Mexican White Oak / Monterrey Oak (Quercus polymorpha)

location.address: Russ Pitman Park / Nature Discovery Center, 7112 Newcastle St, Bellaire, TX 77401

verified_sources: Texas Big Tree Registry, Texas A&M Forest Service, TreeID 2359 (circumference 91 in / 231 cm, spread 65 ft, height 62 ft, condition code 2, owner of record Nature Discovery Center, PublicOrPrivate=1, Display=1, measured May 2020)

naturediscoverycenter.org and bellairetx.gov both independently confirm Russ Pitman Park is a City of Bellaire public park (open 5am-9:30pm daily, free) that hosts the Nature Discovery Center, and describe the park's 'towering oak trees'; the registry's owner field (Nature Discovery Center) matches this site exactly
access: Free. Russ Pitman Park is a City of Bellaire public park, open 5am to 9:30pm every day; the Nature Discovery Center building itself keeps separate, more limited hours, but the park and its trees are open on the park's own hours.
transport: In Bellaire, inside the West Loop (610); roughly 10 km from downtown Houston, drive or bus.
verify_notes: Only ONE source names this exact tree (the registry); two searches for independent coverage of this specific Mexican white oak found only general descriptions of the park's 'towering oak trees' without naming a champion specimen, so per the two-attempts rule this ships flagged rather than chased further. Access itself is solidly double-sourced (the park's own site and the City of Bellaire's own page). No age documented and none derived: no published growth-rate figure for Quercus polymorpha was found this pass. Registry measurement is from May 2020, over five years old but condition code 2 (good) with no news of removal or decline found.
